conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of your circumstances against the official UK government Child Benefit eligibility rules:

## Summary

**You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex, but INELIGIBLE for Blake.**

### For Alex (age 18):
✅ **ELIGIBLE** - You meet all the requirements:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 18 and in approved education (Child Benefit continues for children under 20 in approved education)
- Alex lives with you
- Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week
- Alex hasn't started an apprenticeship in England
- Alex doesn't receive qualifying benefits in their own right
- No other claimant has been identified as having priority

### For Blake (age 17):
❌ **INELIGIBLE** - Although Blake meets the basic criteria (under 20, in approved education, lives with you), another claimant who lives with Blake has priority for claiming Child Benefit. According to the rules, **only one person can get Child Benefit for each child**. Since another claimant has priority, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Blake.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You should use the Child Benefit tax calculator on GOV.UK to check if this applies to you.

According to the eligibility rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child, and if multiple people are responsible, they should agree who will claim, or HMRC will decide. Since another claimant has priority in this case, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Blake.
